binomial.description: This topic covers the binomial distribution, modeling the number of successes in repeated independent trials with a constant success probability. It is widely used in quality control and opinion polling to evaluate proportions. Knowledge of repeated trials and combinations is essential before learning this.

normal.title: Normal distribution
normal.summary: Learn properties and uses of the normal distribution.
normal.description: This topic introduces the bell-shaped normal distribution, teaching standardization techniques and how to calculate probabilities using distribution tables. It is fundamental to statistical inference, standard scores, and experimental error analysis across sciences. Prior knowledge of continuous random variables, mean, and variance is essential.

limit.title: Limits
limit.summary: Find limits of sequences and functions.

sequence.title: Limits of sequences
sequence.summary: Learn how sequence terms behave as the index nears infinity.
sequence.description: This topic examines the behavior of sequences as terms approach infinity, distinguishing between convergence to a limit and divergence. It provides essential tools for evaluating infinite geometric series and modeling discrete dynamical systems. Prior mastery of general sequence formulas, geometric progressions, and inequality manipulation is necessary for this unit.

function.title: Limits of functions
function.summary: Learn function limits near specific points and infinity.
function.description: This topic explores the limits and continuity of functions as the input variable approaches a specific value or infinity. It forms the indispensable foundation for defining derivatives and finding graph asymptotes in calculus. Prior fluency in graphing functions, factoring polynomials, and algebraic manipulation is recommended.

univ-calculus.title: University calculus
univ-calculus.summary: Single-variable calculus at university: the mean value theorem, L'Hôpital's rule and more.

mean-value.title: Mean value theorem & L'Hôpital's rule
mean-value.summary: Learn the Mean Value Theorem and L'Hôpital's Rule.
mean-value.description: This topic covers the Mean Value Theorem, ensuring a point where the tangent slope equals the average rate of change, alongside L'Hôpital's Rule for indeterminate limits. These theorems are essential for proving monotonicity and simplifying complex limits. Prior proficiency in basic derivatives and limits is required.

derivative.title: Differentiation
derivative.summary: Differentiate polynomials to find tangent lines and local extrema.

polynomial.title: Differentiating polynomials
polynomial.summary: Learn how to differentiate polynomial functions using rules.
polynomial.description: This topic focuses on computing derivatives of polynomial functions using power and linearity differentiation rules. Mastered techniques serve as the fundamental groundwork for determining instantaneous rates of change and analyzing graph slopes. A solid background in monomial operations, polynomial algebra, and exponent rules is necessary before starting.

tangent.title: Derivative at a point & tangent lines
tangent.summary: Learn derivatives as slopes and find tangent line equations.
tangent.description: This topic covers the geometric interpretation of the derivative as the slope of a curve, enabling students to construct tangent line equations. It is widely used in linear approximation and analyzing the local directional behavior of curves. Familiarity with polynomial differentiation and line equations from coordinate geometry is required.

extrema.title: Local extrema
extrema.summary: Learn to find local maxima and minima using derivatives.
extrema.description: This topic explores finding local maxima and minima of functions by constructing sign charts of first derivatives. It is vital for graphing functions accurately and solving real-world optimization problems such as maximizing efficiency or minimizing production costs. Prerequisites include differentiating polynomials and solving algebraic inequalities to find critical points.

transcendental.title: Derivatives of trig, exponential and log functions
transcendental.summary: Learn to differentiate trig, exponential, and log functions.
transcendental.description: This topic covers differentiation formulas for trigonometric, natural exponential, and logarithmic functions. These mathematical tools are crucial for modeling periodic wave oscillations, radioactive decay, and dynamic continuous processes in the physical sciences. Students should have a solid foundation in the fundamental properties and standard limits of these functions.

chain-rule.title: Chain, product and quotient rules
chain-rule.summary: Learn the product, quotient, and chain rules of calculus.
chain-rule.description: This topic teaches differentiation rules for product, quotient, and composite functions using the chain rule. These techniques are vital for computing derivatives of intricate formulas arising in physics and economic sensitivity analysis. A firm grasp of differentiating elementary polynomial and transcendental functions is essential prior knowledge.

parametric.title: Derivatives of parametric functions
parametric.summary: Learn to differentiate parametric curves to find slopes.
parametric.description: This topic covers finding the derivative dy/dx of curves defined parametrically using the chain rule. It is essential for determining slopes, tangent vectors, and trajectories of geometric curves like cycloids and ellipses in kinematics. Prerequisites include a firm understanding of parametric representations and single-variable differentiation techniques.

motion.title: Velocity & acceleration
motion.summary: Learn to find velocity and acceleration using derivatives.
motion.description: This topic demonstrates calculating velocity and acceleration by taking the first and second derivatives of a position function with respect to time. It is an indispensable tool in classical mechanics and engineering simulations for describing motion. Students should be proficient in differentiating polynomial and trigonometric functions before taking this module.

integral.title: Integration
integral.summary: Practice indefinite and definite integrals and use them to find areas.

indefinite.title: Indefinite integrals
indefinite.summary: Learn to compute indefinite integrals as antiderivatives.
indefinite.description: This topic explores finding indefinite integrals with integration constants, serving as the reverse operation of differentiation. It forms the foundational calculation technique for reconstructing total quantities from rates of change and computing definite integrals. A solid grasp of polynomial differentiation rules and algebraic manipulation is required before beginning.

definite.title: Definite integrals
definite.summary: Learn to compute definite integrals over given intervals.
definite.description: This topic covers evaluating definite integrals by substituting the upper and lower limits into an antiderivative and taking their difference. It is widely applied in calculating geometric areas, volumes, and physical work. Prior familiarity with finding antiderivatives and algebraic substitution is necessary.

area.title: Area
area.summary: Find areas enclosed by curves using definite integrals.
area.description: Learn to calculate areas enclosed between curves and lines by integrating the difference between upper and lower functions over the corresponding interval. This method is widely applied in geometric measurements and engineering analysis. Mastery of definite integral calculations and finding intersection points of graphs is recommended.

substitution.title: Integration by substitution
substitution.summary: Learn techniques of integration by substitution.
substitution.description: Learn integration by substitution, which rewrites an integral by replacing part of the expression with a new variable and using derivative relations. This technique is widely used for solving differential equations and calculating complex areas and volumes. Prior knowledge of the chain rule and basic indefinite integrals is required.

by-parts.title: Integration by parts
by-parts.summary: Learn integration by parts for products of functions.
by-parts.description: This section covers integration by parts, a technique derived from the product rule of differentiation. It is widely used to integrate products of polynomials, exponential, and trigonometric functions. A solid understanding of the product rule and basic indefinite integration will help you master this method.

volume.title: Volumes and arc length
volume.summary: Compute volumes and arc lengths using definite integrals.
volume.description: In this section, you will learn how to calculate solid volumes, volumes of revolution, and arc lengths using definite integrals. These techniques are essential for geometric measurements and physical modeling. A solid grasp of basic definite integration and derivatives is recommended before starting this topic.

complex.title: Complex numbers
complex.summary: Practice complex arithmetic, non-real roots of quadratic equations, and the complex plane.

arithmetic.title: Complex arithmetic
arithmetic.summary: Learn the imaginary unit and complex arithmetic operations.
arithmetic.description: This section introduces the imaginary unit and covers the fundamental rules for adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing complex numbers. These arithmetic skills are widely used in advanced algebra, physics, and engineering. Familiarity with real number arithmetic, polynomial expansion, and rationalizing denominators is helpful beforehand.

quadratic-roots.title: Non-real roots of quadratic equations
quadratic-roots.summary: Find complex solutions of quadratic equations.
quadratic-roots.description: This section explores finding complex roots for quadratic equations when the discriminant is negative by extending the quadratic formula. It ensures that every quadratic equation has solutions, leading to deeper algebraic concepts. Before starting, you should be familiar with the real quadratic formula and basic complex arithmetic.

plane.title: The complex plane
plane.summary: Represent complex numbers geometrically on the complex plane.
plane.description: In this section, you will learn to represent complex numbers as points on a plane, using polar form and De Moivre's theorem. This approach connects algebra with geometry, allowing rotations and scalings to be computed easily. Basic knowledge of complex arithmetic and trigonometry is essential prior to this topic.

coordinate-geometry.title: Coordinate geometry
coordinate-geometry.summary: Practice equations of lines and circles, and loci.

line.title: Equations of lines
line.summary: Formulate and analyze equations of lines in the plane.
line.description: This section covers various forms of linear equations, parallel and perpendicular conditions, and the distance formula from a point to a line. It provides the foundation for solving geometric problems using algebra on the coordinate plane. Prior knowledge of linear functions, slopes, and Cartesian coordinates is recommended.

circle.title: Equations of circles
circle.summary: Determine equations of circles and analyze intersections.
circle.description: This section focuses on deriving the equation of a circle from its center and radius, as well as finding tangents and intersection points with lines. It is widely used to analyze circular curves and geometric tangency algebraically. Familiarity with the distance formula and linear equations is recommended beforehand.

locus.title: Loci
locus.summary: Find equations of loci traced by points under conditions.
locus.description: This section covers methods for finding the algebraic equation of a locus, which is the path traced by a moving point satisfying given geometric conditions. This skill is vital for translating dynamic geometric constraints into equations. A good command of the distance formula, lines, and circle equations is helpful beforehand.

region.title: Regions defined by inequalities
region.summary: Graph regions defined by inequalities in the plane.
region.description: This section teaches how to graph regions represented by inequalities on the coordinate plane and solve optimization problems like linear programming. These graphical methods are widely used to identify feasible regions under constraints. Prior familiarity with linear equations, circle equations, and basic inequality properties is recommended.

vector.title: Vectors
vector.summary: Practice vector components and magnitude, dot products, and angles between vectors.

components.title: Components & magnitude
components.summary: Represent vectors by components and compute magnitudes.
components.description: In this section, you will learn to represent geometric vectors using coordinate components and calculate their magnitudes, additions, and scalar multiplications. This algebraic representation simplifies vector operations in physics and geometry. Basic understanding of geometric vectors and the Pythagorean theorem is recommended beforehand.

dot-product.title: Dot products
dot-product.summary: Learn the definition and properties of the dot product.
dot-product.description: This section covers the definition of the dot product using vector magnitudes and angles, as well as its algebraic computation via components. It is essential for checking orthogonality and calculating mechanical work in physics. Prior familiarity with vector components, magnitudes, and cosine values from trigonometry is required.

angle.title: Angles between vectors
angle.summary: Determine the angle between vectors using dot products.
angle.description: Learn how to find the cosine of the angle between two vectors using their magnitudes and dot product. This method is widely used to analyze directional relationships in two- and three-dimensional spaces. Familiarity with vector magnitudes, dot product calculations, and fundamental trigonometry is required.

space.title: Vectors in space
space.summary: Extend vectors to three-dimensional space and coordinates.
space.description: This section extends vector concepts into three-dimensional space, covering 3D coordinate components, dot products, and equations of geometric figures. These tools are indispensable for 3D computer graphics, physics simulations, and solid geometry. Prior proficiency in 2D vector arithmetic and dot products is strongly recommended.

matrix.title: Matrices
matrix.summary: Practice matrix addition and multiplication, 2×2 determinants, and inverse matrices.

operations.title: Matrix addition & multiplication
operations.summary: Learn fundamental operations of matrix addition and product.
operations.description: This section introduces the definition of matrices along with the rules for matrix addition, scalar multiplication, and matrix multiplication. These operations are fundamental for representing linear transformations and systems of equations compactly. Familiarity with basic arithmetic and the dot product of vectors will facilitate your understanding.

determinant.title: 2×2 determinants
determinant.summary: Compute 2x2 determinants and understand their meaning.
determinant.description: This section covers the definition of the 2x2 determinant, its geometric interpretation as signed area, and its role in testing matrix invertibility. Determinants are crucial for determining whether inverse matrices exist and solving linear systems. Prior understanding of matrix notation and basic plane geometry is recommended.

general-determinant.title: n×n determinants: cofactors & Cramer's rule
general-determinant.summary: Learn n-th order determinants and Cramer's rule.
general-determinant.description: Learn the properties of general n-th order determinants, calculation via cofactor expansion, and Cramer's rule. These tools are widely applied to solve linear systems with many unknowns and to formulate eigenvalue problems. Prior proficiency in evaluating 2x2 determinants and performing basic matrix operations is required.

inverse.title: Inverse matrices
inverse.summary: Understand definition and computation of inverse matrices.
inverse.description: This section covers the definition of inverse matrices, invertibility criteria via determinants, and explicit computational formulas. Inverse matrices are essential tools for solving matrix equations and performing coordinate transformations in geometry. Familiarity with matrix multiplication, identity matrices, and determinant calculations is required beforehand.

linear-system.title: Linear systems & matrices
linear-system.summary: Solve systems of linear equations using row reduction and determine the number of solutions.

elimination.title: Row reduction
elimination.summary: Solve linear systems using Gaussian elimination methods.
elimination.description: This section covers Gaussian and Gauss-Jordan elimination, solving systems of linear equations systematically via elementary row operations on augmented matrices. It provides an efficient algorithmic approach for handling large systems and computing inverses. Prior knowledge of elementary algebra and basic matrix notation is recommended.

solutions.title: Number of solutions
solutions.summary: Determine the number of solutions to a linear system.
solutions.description: Learn how to determine the number of solutions by comparing the ranks of the coefficient and augmented matrices with the number of unknowns. If the ranks are equal, the system has a unique solution when equal to the unknowns, or infinitely many when smaller. Understanding elementary row operations is required.

vector-space.title: Vector spaces
vector-space.summary: Linear independence, bases and dimension, and matrix rank.

independence.title: Linear independence
independence.summary: Learn linear independence and dependence of vectors.
independence.description: This section covers the precise definition and criteria for linear independence and linear dependence among a set of vectors. This concept is fundamental for defining bases and dimension in vector spaces without redundancy. Prior knowledge of vector linear combinations and techniques for solving linear systems is essential.

basis.title: Basis and dimension
basis.summary: Learn the basis and dimension of vector spaces.
basis.description: Learn the concepts of a basis, which spans a vector space with linearly independent vectors, and dimension, representing the number of basis vectors. These are essential for understanding degrees of freedom in vector spaces. Familiarity with linear combinations and linear independence is helpful.

rank.title: Rank
rank.summary: Learn the rank of a matrix and its meaning.
rank.description: Learn the rank of a matrix, defined as the maximum number of linearly independent row or column vectors. It is widely used to determine the solvability and degrees of freedom of linear systems. Prior knowledge of elementary row operations and linear independence is helpful.

linear-map.title: Linear maps
linear-map.summary: Find matrix representations, kernels and images.

matrix-rep.title: Matrix representation
matrix-rep.summary: Learn matrix representations of linear maps.
matrix-rep.description: Learn how to represent linear mappings as matrices by choosing bases for vector spaces. This technique allows abstract linear transformations to be computed concretely using matrix algebra. Prior knowledge of the definition of linear maps and vector space bases is recommended.

kernel-image.title: Kernel and image
kernel-image.summary: Learn the kernel and image of linear maps.
kernel-image.description: Learn about the kernel, which consists of vectors mapped to zero, and the image, representing all possible outputs. These spaces are fundamental for analyzing linear transformations through the rank-nullity theorem. Prior understanding of linear maps and systems of linear equations is helpful.

eigen.title: Eigenvalues & eigenvectors
eigen.summary: Practice finding eigenvalues and eigenvectors of 2×2 matrices.

eigenvalues.title: 2×2 eigenvalues
eigenvalues.summary: Learn how to find eigenvalues of 2x2 matrices.
eigenvalues.description: Learn how to calculate the eigenvalues of a 2x2 matrix by solving its characteristic equation. An eigenvalue represents the scalar factor by which a nonzero vector is scaled under a linear transformation. Prior understanding of determinants and quadratic equation solving methods is required.

eigenvectors.title: Eigenvectors
eigenvectors.summary: Learn how to find eigenvectors for given eigenvalues.
eigenvectors.description: Learn how to find eigenvectors, which are nonzero vectors that become their own scalar multiples scaled by the corresponding eigenvalues when multiplied by the matrix. These vectors are widely applied in principal component analysis and vibration engineering. Knowledge of solving linear systems and finding eigenvalues is required.

diagonalize.title: Diagonalization
diagonalize.summary: Learn how to diagonalize square matrices.
diagonalize.description: Learn how to transform square matrices into diagonal matrices using eigenvectors and invertible matrices. Diagonalization is extremely useful for computing matrix powers and solving systems of differential equations. Prior mastery of finding eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and matrix inverses is necessary.

inner-product.title: Inner products & orthogonality
inner-product.summary: Orthogonal and orthonormal bases, and Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization.

orthogonal.title: Orthogonal and orthonormal bases
orthogonal.description: Learn to define orthogonality using inner products and construct orthonormal bases consisting of mutually perpendicular unit vectors. These bases are fundamental in geometric projections and data analysis. Prior understanding of inner products, vector norms, and bases is recommended.

gram-schmidt.title: Gram-Schmidt process
gram-schmidt.description: Learn the algorithm to construct an orthonormal basis for the subspace spanned by a set of linearly independent vectors. This method is fundamental for matrix QR decomposition and generating systems of orthogonal functions. Understanding inner products, vector projections, and vector space bases is required.

rate.title: Speed & unit rates
rate.summary: Find speed, time and distance, and compare quantities per unit.

speed.title: Speed, time and distance
speed.summary: Learn the relations of speed, time, and distance.
speed.description: Learn the relationships among speed, time, and distance, and how to calculate each quantity using formulas. This concept is useful in daily life for estimating travel times and distances. A solid foundation in basic multiplication and division is helpful before beginning.

per-unit.title: Unit rates
per-unit.summary: Learn to calculate and compare quantities per unit.
per-unit.description: Learn how to compare quantities by standardizing amounts to a single unit, such as population density. This method helps compare crowdedness or efficiency across groups of different sizes. Basic understanding of division and operations with decimal numbers is required beforehand.

relations.title: Changing quantities & proportion
relations.summary: How two quantities change together, up to direct and inverse proportion.

change.title: Quantities that change together
change.summary: Learn relationships between two changing quantities.
change.description: Learn how to observe how one quantity changes as another changes by organizing data into tables. This foundational skill helps students discover mathematical rules and prepare for studying functions. Prior ability to read tables and perform basic arithmetic is recommended.

simple-proportion.title: Simple proportion
simple-proportion.summary: Learn simple proportional relationships and tables.
simple-proportion.description: Learn the relationship where one quantity doubles or triples as the other quantity doubles or triples. This concept is useful in daily life, such as calculating total costs based on quantities purchased. Prior knowledge of basic changing quantities and multiplication is essential.

proportion.title: Direct & inverse proportion
proportion.summary: Learn properties of direct and inverse proportion.
proportion.description: Learn the properties, formulas, and graphs of direct and inverse proportion, where ratios or products remain constant. These relationships are widely used to model quantitative phenomena in science and economics. Prior understanding of expressions with variables and fractions or decimals is helpful.

angles.title: Angles & polygons
angles.summary: Find angles with parallel lines and the interior and exterior angles of polygons.

parallel.title: Angles and parallel lines
parallel.summary: Learn angles formed by parallel lines and a line.
parallel.description: Learn the geometric properties of corresponding and alternate interior angles formed when a transversal intersects parallel lines. This knowledge is essential for calculating unknown angles and proving geometric properties. Familiarity with straight line angles and vertically opposite angles is helpful.

polygon.title: Interior and exterior angles
polygon.summary: Learn interior and exterior angles of polygons.
polygon.description: Learn how to calculate the sum of interior angles by dividing polygons into triangles, and understand why exterior angles always sum to 360 degrees. This is useful for analyzing regular polygons and architectural shapes. Prior knowledge of triangle angle sums being 180 degrees is required.

congruence.title: Congruence & properties of shapes
congruence.summary: Congruence conditions for triangles, and properties of isosceles triangles and parallelograms.

conditions.title: Congruence conditions
conditions.summary: Learn conditions for congruence of triangles.
conditions.description: Learn the three conditions for triangle congruence based on the equality of corresponding sides and angles. These conditions form the core foundation for proving various geometric theorems logically. Familiarity with the basic parts of triangles and geometric constructions is helpful before studying this topic.

triangles.title: Isosceles & right triangles
triangles.summary: Learn isosceles and right triangle properties.
triangles.description: Learn the properties of isosceles triangles, such as equal base angles, and the special congruence conditions for right triangles involving the hypotenuse. These are frequently applied in geometric proofs and length calculations. Prior mastery of general triangle congruence conditions is required.

parallelogram.title: Conditions for parallelograms
parallelogram.summary: Learn conditions for being a parallelogram.
parallelogram.description: Learn the conditions that determine whether a quadrilateral is a parallelogram based on opposite sides, opposite angles, and diagonals. This concept is essential for classifying shapes and conducting advanced geometric proofs. Prior understanding of triangle congruence proofs and parallel line properties is required.

circle-solid.title: Circles & solids
circle-solid.summary: Sectors, and the volume and surface area of cones, pyramids and spheres.

solid-views.title: Sketches, nets & projections of solids
solid-views.summary: Learn sketches, nets, and projections of solids.
solid-views.description: Learn how to represent three-dimensional solids on two-dimensional surfaces using sketches, nets, and orthographic projections. These representations are essential for calculating surface areas and reading design drawings. Prior familiarity with basic plane figures and basic solid geometric shapes is recommended.

sector.title: Sectors
sector.summary: Find the arc length and area of a circular sector.
sector.description: Learn how to calculate the arc length and area of a sector using its radius and central angle. This topic builds on the formulas for the circumference and area of a circle using ratios. It is widely used in geometric measurement, such as unfolding solids and finding composite areas.

solid.title: Volume and surface area of solids
solid.summary: Calculate volume and surface area of pyramids and spheres.
solid.description: Learn the formulas to calculate the volume and surface area of pyramids, cones, and spheres. This topic builds on previous knowledge of prisms, cylinders, and circles. These skills are essential for solving real-world 3D geometry problems, such as determining capacity and designing spatial models.

similarity.title: Similarity & circle theorems
similarity.summary: Use similar figures and the inscribed angle theorem.

similarity.title: Similar figures
similarity.summary: Learn properties and ratios of similar figures.
similarity.description: Learn the definition and conditions of geometric similarity and how shapes scale proportionally. This builds on basic ratio concepts and triangle congruence to find unknown lengths, area ratios, and volume ratios. It is widely used in practical applications like reading maps and measuring heights indirectly.

inscribed-angle.title: Inscribed angle theorem
inscribed-angle.summary: Learn the inscribed angle theorem and angle relations.
inscribed-angle.description: Explore the relationship between inscribed angles and central angles subtended by the same arc. Building on basic angle properties and isosceles triangles, this concept is used to calculate unknown angles and determine concyclic points. It is an indispensable tool for geometric proofs and circle constructions.

transformations.title: Transformations
transformations.summary: Move figures by translation, rotation and reflection.

moves.title: Translations, rotations and reflections
moves.summary: Learn translation, rotation, and reflection of shapes.
moves.description: Understand how shapes change position and orientation through translations, rotations, and reflections. This topic builds on basic concepts of points, line segments, and angles, emphasizing that size and shape are preserved. These transformations are widely used in tessellations, graphic design, and advanced geometric analysis.

geometric-reasoning.title: Constructions & proofs
geometric-reasoning.summary: Basic constructions, and how proofs with congruence, similarity and inscribed angles go.

construction.title: Basic constructions
construction.summary: Learn compass and straightedge geometric constructions.
construction.description: Learn how to construct perpendicular bisectors, angle bisectors, and perpendicular lines using only a compass and straightedge. This requires understanding the properties of circles and equidistant points. Geometric construction is widely used to locate points satisfying specific geometric conditions and to verify geometric theorems.

congruence-proof.title: Proofs with congruent triangles
congruence-proof.summary: Prove geometric properties using triangle congruence.
congruence-proof.description: Learn how to construct deductive proofs for geometric properties and congruent segments or angles using triangle congruence conditions. Proofs are written step by step based on properties of vertical angles and alternate interior angles. This topic fosters logical reasoning skills and serves as a foundation for geometric exploration.

similarity-proof.title: Proofs with similar triangles
similarity-proof.summary: Prove segment ratios and equal angles using similarity.
similarity-proof.description: Learn how to construct logical proofs establishing segment ratios and equal angles based on triangle similarity criteria. This method builds on parallel line properties and congruence proofs by focusing on proportional sides and corresponding angles. It is essential for solving complex geometry problems and analyzing spatial relationships.

circle-proof.title: Proofs with inscribed angles
circle-proof.summary: Prove circle properties with inscribed angle theorems.
circle-proof.description: Learn how to prove geometric relationships using the inscribed angle theorem, its converse, and cyclic quadrilaterals. This builds on congruence and similarity proofs, combining angle relationships with circle geometry. These proofs are frequently used to solve intricate geometric problems involving circles and concyclic points.

triangle-trig.title: Solving triangles
triangle-trig.summary: Find sides, angles and areas of triangles with the laws of sines and cosines.

ratios.title: Trigonometric ratios
ratios.summary: Learn definitions of sine, cosine, and tangent ratios.
ratios.description: Understand definitions and identities of sine, cosine, and tangent based on right triangles. Building on triangle similarity and the Pythagorean theorem, learners calculate unknown side lengths from an angle and a known side. These ratios are foundational for surveying, physics, and vector decomposition.

sine-law.title: Law of sines
sine-law.summary: Apply the Law of Sines to find sides, angles, and radii.
sine-law.description: Learn the Law of Sines, which relates the sides and opposing angles of a triangle to its circumcircle radius. Building on basic trigonometric ratios and the inscribed angle theorem, it determines unknown lengths and angles. It is widely applied in surveying, navigation, and solving oblique triangles.

cosine-law.title: Law of cosines
cosine-law.summary: Apply the Law of Cosines to solve oblique triangles.
cosine-law.description: Understand the Law of Cosines, which connects the three sides of any triangle with the cosine of one angle. As a generalization of the Pythagorean theorem, this rule requires basic trigonometric concepts. It is essential for determining unknown lengths and angles in surveying, 3D modeling, and vector calculations.

area.title: Area of a triangle
area.summary: Calculate triangle area using trigonometric formulas.
area.description: Learn how to calculate triangle area using two sides and the sine of the included angle, as well as the inradius. This builds upon basic area concepts and trigonometric ratios to solve oblique triangles. It is widely used in land surveying, computer graphics, and decomposing polygons into measurable parts.

triangle-properties.title: Properties of figures
triangle-properties.summary: Triangle centers, the power of a point, and Ceva's and Menelaus's theorems.

centers.title: Triangle centers
centers.summary: Learn definitions and properties of triangle centers.
centers.description: Study the definitions and geometric properties of the five triangle centers: circumcenter, incenter, centroid, orthocenter, and excenters. This topic requires foundational knowledge of angle bisectors, medians, and perpendiculars. These concepts are essential for advanced Euclidean geometry, structural balancing in mechanics, and analyzing geometric configurations.

power.title: Power of a point
power.summary: Apply the Power of a Point theorem to circles and lines.
power.description: Understand the Power of a Point theorem, relating line segments formed by intersecting chords, secants, and tangents of circles. This topic relies on prior knowledge of triangle similarity and inscribed angle properties. It is a powerful tool for calculating unknown lengths in circle geometry and solving advanced proofs.

ceva-menelaus.title: Ceva's and Menelaus's theorems
ceva-menelaus.summary: Apply Ceva's and Menelaus's theorems to segment ratios.
ceva-menelaus.description: Learn ratio relationships that hold when three lines through triangle vertices meet at one point, or when a line intersects three sides or their extensions. Using similarity and ratios, these theorems efficiently compute complex line segments. They are widely utilized in analyzing geometric figures.

polyhedra.title: Polyhedra
polyhedra.summary: Study regular polyhedra and Euler's polyhedron formula.
polyhedra.description: Explore the geometric properties and symmetries of the five Platonic solids, along with Euler's polyhedron formula relating vertices, edges, and faces. This topic builds on basic spatial concepts and regular polygons. It is applied in analyzing molecular crystal structures, 3D computer graphics, and architectural design.

construction.title: Geometric constructions
construction.summary: Master geometric constructions using geometric theorems.
construction.description: Learn construction techniques based on geometric theorems, such as dividing segments proportionally, constructing square root lengths, and drawing circle tangents. This topic combines basic straightedge and compass methods with properties of similarity and inscribed angles. It is widely utilized in architectural drafting and geometric investigation.

quartiles.title: Quartiles & box plots
quartiles.summary: Find quartiles and read the spread of data from box plots.

quartiles.title: Quartiles
quartiles.summary: Calculate quartiles and measure data dispersion.
quartiles.description: Learn how to calculate quartiles that divide ordered data into four equal parts, recognizing that the second quartile corresponds to the median. By using the interquartile range, you will quantify the dispersion and spread of data distributions. This concept is widely applied in statistics to objectively compare variability across different datasets.

boxplot.title: Box plots
boxplot.summary: Use boxplots to assess data spread and compare datasets.
boxplot.description: Learn how to construct boxplots using minimum, maximum, and quartile values to analyze data spread and compare multiple groups. By visualizing summary statistics, boxplots clearly illustrate the skewness and variability of distributions. This technique is widely utilized to compare trends across experimental and survey datasets.

frequency.title: Frequency distributions
frequency.summary: Reading frequency tables and histograms, and finding relative frequencies.

frequency.title: Frequency tables & relative frequency
frequency.summary: Learn frequency distributions and relative frequencies.
frequency.description: You will learn how to organize data into frequency distribution tables and histograms, and calculate relative frequencies. This is essential for visualizing and understanding how data is distributed. A good understanding of basic decimal arithmetic and percentages will help you master these concepts.

sampling.title: Sampling
sampling.summary: Census versus sampling, and estimating a population from a sample.

population-sample.title: Populations & samples
population-sample.summary: Learn populations, samples, and random sampling basics.
population-sample.description: You will learn the difference between censuses and sample surveys, as well as the concept of random sampling. This approach is widely used in opinion polls and quality control where surveying the whole population is impractical. Prior knowledge of organizing basic statistical data will support your learning.

estimate.title: Estimating from a sample
estimate.summary: Estimate population values from sample statistics.
estimate.description: You will learn how to estimate population parameters from sample statistics using proportions and proportional reasoning. This technique is widely applied to estimate wildlife populations and product defect rates. Familiarity with solving ratios and proportional equations will make these concepts much easier to understand.

statistics.title: Variance & correlation
statistics.summary: Find the variance, standard deviation and correlation coefficient.

variance.title: Variance and standard deviation
variance.summary: Learn how to calculate variance and standard deviation.
variance.description: You will learn to measure data dispersion by calculating variance, the mean of squared deviations, and standard deviation. These statistics are essential for analyzing fluctuations in test scores and measurement errors. Prior knowledge of calculating the mean and basic operations with square roots will be very helpful.

correlation.title: Correlation coefficient
correlation.summary: Learn the correlation coefficient between two variables.
correlation.description: You will learn how to quantify the linear relationship between two variables using scatter plots and the correlation coefficient. It is widely used to analyze whether two factors, like height and weight, are related. Prior knowledge of calculating variance and standard deviation will help you follow this topic smoothly.

hypothesis.title: The idea of hypothesis testing
hypothesis.summary: Learn the logic and principles of hypothesis testing.
hypothesis.description: Learn hypothesis testing by evaluating the probability of observing results as extreme as or more extreme than the actual outcome under a null hypothesis. Unlike strict mathematical contradiction, probabilistic decisions inherently carry a risk of error. This statistical framework is widely applied in clinical trials and quality management.

inference.title: Estimation & hypothesis testing
inference.summary: Estimate means and proportions and carry out hypothesis tests.

random-variables.title: Random variables & distributions
random-variables.summary: Learn random variables, distributions, and variance.
random-variables.description: Learn about random variables whose values are determined by trial outcomes, their probability distributions, and how to compute expectation and variance. These concepts quantify central tendency and dispersion, forming the foundation for statistical inference. Prior understanding of basic probability rules and sequence summations is required.

estimation.title: Estimation
estimation.summary: Learn parameter estimation using confidence intervals.
estimation.description: You will learn how to estimate population means and proportions within intervals based on a specified confidence level using sample statistics. This technique is indispensable in opinion polling and industrial quality control. A solid understanding of the normal distribution and sample means will be beneficial.

testing.title: Hypothesis testing
testing.summary: Learn hypothesis testing and significance levels.
testing.description: You will learn how to set null and alternative hypotheses, calculate test statistics, and determine rejection using significance levels. This method is widely used in comparing product performance and determining scientific significance. Familiarity with the normal distribution and interval estimation will help you master this topic.

sets.title: Sets
sets.summary: Unions, intersections and complements, and counting with Venn diagrams.

operations.title: Union, intersection and complement
operations.summary: Learn unions, intersections, and complements of sets.
operations.description: You will learn set notation, how to find unions and intersections of sets, and how to determine the complement within a universal set. These fundamental tools are essential across mathematics for classifying objects based on given conditions. Basic knowledge of numbers and inequalities will help you grasp these concepts quickly.

venn.title: Venn diagrams and counting
venn.summary: Learn to use Venn diagrams and count set elements.
venn.description: You will learn how to visualize overlapping sets using Venn diagrams and calculate element counts with the inclusion-exclusion principle. This technique is widely used in survey data analysis and combinatorial counting. Prior familiarity with basic set operations like unions and intersections will be very beneficial.

logic.title: Propositions & logic
logic.summary: Negation and contrapositive, necessary and sufficient conditions, and truth tables.

negation.title: Negation and contrapositive
negation.summary: Learn negation, contrapositives, and indirect proofs.
negation.description: You will learn how to formulate negations, converses, inverses, and contrapositives of propositions, exploring why a statement shares its truth value with its contrapositive. This concept is crucial for proving mathematical statements indirectly. Understanding basic set relationships and deductive reasoning will support your progress.

conditions.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions
conditions.summary: Learn necessary, sufficient, and equivalent conditions.
conditions.description: You will learn how to identify necessary conditions, sufficient conditions, and equivalences by examining implications between statements. This provides precision when verifying solutions to equations and stating assumptions of mathematical theorems. Familiarity with determining truth values of propositions and set inclusions will be helpful.

truth-table.title: Truth tables
truth-table.summary: Learn truth tables to evaluate compound propositions.
truth-table.description: You will learn to construct truth tables for logical operators such as conjunction, disjunction, negation, and implication to determine the validity of compound propositions. This skill is widely applied in logic circuit design and verifying program branching conditions. Basic knowledge of logical operations and set theory will be beneficial.

mapping.title: Functions & relations
mapping.summary: Injective and surjective maps, and equivalence relations.

injective.title: Injective and surjective maps
injective.summary: Learn injective, surjective, and bijective mappings.
injective.description: You will learn the formal definitions of injective, surjective, and bijective mappings, as well as the conditions required for inverse mappings to exist. These concepts are fundamental in modern algebra and invertible data transformations in computer science. Prior familiarity with functions and basic set operations will support your progress.

equivalence.title: Equivalence relations
equivalence.summary: Learn equivalence relations, properties, and partitions.
equivalence.description: You will learn about relations satisfying reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity, and how equivalence classes partition a set into disjoint subsets. This forms the foundation for modern algebraic concepts such as modular arithmetic and quotient structures. A solid grasp of Cartesian products and logical deductions will be advantageous.

series.title: Series & Taylor expansions
series.summary: Sums and convergence of series, and Taylor expansions.

series.title: Sums and convergence of series
series.summary: Learn convergence tests and partial sums of infinite series.
series.description: You will learn how infinite series are defined as limits of partial sums and how to determine convergence using standard tests. This forms the foundation for series representations and polynomial approximations of functions, as well as stability analysis in physics. A solid command of sequence limits and geometric series formulas is essential.

taylor.title: Taylor expansions
taylor.summary: Learn Taylor polynomials and series expansions.
taylor.description: You will learn how to approximate functions locally with polynomials using higher-order derivatives, as well as power series representations through Taylor and Maclaurin expansions. This approach is widely applied in numerical computation and physical modeling. A solid grasp of higher-order differentiation and series convergence is essential.

improper-integral.title: Improper integrals
improper-integral.summary: Integrals over infinite intervals or with singularities.

improper.title: Improper integrals
improper.summary: Learn to evaluate improper integrals using limits.
improper.description: You will learn how to evaluate improper integrals where the interval of integration extends to infinity or the integrand has singularities, using limit processes. These integrals are extensively used in computing expectations of continuous random variables and physical potentials. Proficiency in definite integrals and limits is required.

multivariable.title: Partial derivatives & multiple integrals
multivariable.summary: Partial derivatives and multiple integrals of functions of several variables.

partial.title: Partial derivatives
partial.summary: Learn partial derivatives of multivariable functions.
partial.description: You will learn how to compute partial derivatives of multivariable functions by differentiating with respect to one variable while treating others as constants. This method is fundamental in solving multivariable optimization problems and analyzing physical fields. Mastery of single-variable differentiation rules is an essential prerequisite.

double-integral.title: Multiple integrals
double-integral.summary: Learn how to calculate double integrals in the plane.
double-integral.description: Learn to calculate double integrals of functions of two variables over planar regions. They are widely used to determine the volume under surfaces and the area of two-dimensional shapes. A solid foundation in single-variable definite integration and iterated integrals is recommended before starting.

polar.title: Change to polar coordinates
polar.summary: Learn to compute double integrals in polar coordinates.
polar.description: Learn how to transform double integrals from Cartesian to polar coordinates using the Jacobian determinant. This technique is particularly useful for simplifying integrals over circular or symmetric regions. Before studying this topic, familiarity with basic double integrals and trigonometry is recommended.

ode.title: Differential equations
ode.summary: Solve separable, first-order linear and constant-coefficient second-order equations.

separable.title: Separable equations
separable.summary: Learn how to solve separable differential equations.
separable.description: Learn how to solve separable differential equations by separating the variables onto opposite sides and integrating. This method is frequently applied to model physical phenomena like population growth and radioactive decay. Before starting, you should have a solid grasp of basic derivative rules and indefinite integration.

linear-first.title: First-order linear equations
linear-first.summary: Learn to solve first-order linear differential equations.
linear-first.description: Learn techniques for solving first-order linear differential equations, including integrating factors and variation of parameters. These equations are widely used to analyze electric circuits and mixing processes in engineering and physics. Prior mastery of the product rule for differentiation and standard integration techniques is essential.

second-order.title: Second-order with constant coefficients
second-order.summary: Solve second-order linear ODEs with constant coefficients.
second-order.description: Learn how to solve second-order linear differential equations with constant coefficients using characteristic equations. They are fundamental in modeling oscillatory phenomena, such as spring vibrations and alternating current circuits. Prior knowledge of solving quadratic equations and differentiating exponential functions is recommended.
